title: Dynamic Memory and Ownership Basics
learningObjectives: Explain dynamic memory and ownership basics.
Describe pointer/reference or lifetime rules involved.
Trace a simple memory access or ownership operation.
Recognize common undefined behavior and safety risks.
Choose a safer approach for a practical task.

understand.concept: Dynamic storage can outlive a scope but must have clear ownership. Raw new/delete are error-prone; prefer RAII objects and containers. Avoid mismatched delete forms and leaks.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding dynamic allocation explains heap lifetime and why modern C++ uses managed ownership.
understand.explain: Match allocation/deallocation and prefer standard containers or smart pointers to manage lifetime automatically.

examples.title: Automatic lifetime
examples.explanation: local is alive during the pointer use; no delete is needed.

examples.title: Avoid manual ownership
examples.explanation: Container manages its allocation and cleanup.

examples.title: RAII file object
examples.code: std::ifstream file(\"input.txt\");\n// file closes when object leaves scope
examples.explanation: RAII object manages resource cleanup; include fstream.

examples.title: Manual allocation caution
examples.explanation: Illustrates matching new/delete; prefer smart pointers in modern code.

examples.title: Array allocation form
examples.code: int* p=new int[3]{1,2,3};\n// release with delete[] p;
examples.explanation: Array new must be paired with delete[]; avoid raw ownership.

practise.guidedTask: Trace the five Dynamic Memory and Ownership Basics examples. Mark each pointer/reference's target, object lifetime, mutability and whether dereferencing is valid.
practise.independentTask: Build a small C++ exercise showing dynamic memory and ownership basics. Include safe cases and deliberately describe (but do not execute) one invalid case. Demonstrate how ownership or lifetime is managed.
hints: Draw pointer arrows to live objects.
Use nullptr for empty pointers and check before dereferencing.
Keep pointer arithmetic within one array.
Distinguish pointer constness from pointee constness.
Prefer value returns, containers and smart pointers to manual ownership.

questions.explanation: Local objects are destroyed when scope exits.
Resource cleanup is managed by object lifetime.
Scalar new pairs with scalar delete.
RAII containers/smart pointers reduce manual cleanup.
